newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed, focus on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed, focus on jobs data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Thursday, with the money market focused on the release on Friday of key Canadian and U.S. job reports, analysts said.

"The market is somewhat tentative in front of the employment reports tomorrow in both Canada and the U.S. The longer end of the market is just kind of sitting there because of that," said one T-bill dealer with a Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield of 2.98 percent, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.
Fixed-income investors will be studying the employment reports for evidence of inflation growth in both countries and clues about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will soon hike rates.
Meanwhile, many T-bill investors and traders were taking a cautious stance, analysts said.

"Most of the bill maturities, the customer business, has tended to be in that two to six month area, so maturities are just being rolled very short. Most investors are approaching it fairly cautiously," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield of 3.33 percent, unchanged from Wednesday. The one-year T-bill also tradeed unchanged to yield 3.81 percent.

The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.10 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range. Dealers said the call loan rate was being affected by settlement pressures from Tuesday's weekly T-bill auction.
